blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corp. (Pagcor) reported an 85 percent drop in net income in the first nine months of the year, as weaker gaming revenues and higher remittances for government nation-building projects weighed on earnings. The state-run gaming regulator said in a statement that net income fell to P2.17 billion in the January-to-September period. READ: BIZ BUZZ: Pagcor bets on app to curb illegal gambling Total revenues declined 23.41 percent year-on-year to P64.41 billion, reflecting softer earnings from gaming operations and related services.
